recent_posts.title: What's New in InfluxDB 3 Explorer 1.8: Streaming Subscriptions, Smarter Sample Data, Line Protocol Validation, and Retention Controls
recent_posts.summary: InfluxDB 3 Explorer 1.8 introduces several new features for writing and managing time-series data. The release adds a Data Subscriptions page for streaming data directly from MQTT, Kafka, and AMQP sources into databases. Sample data capabilities are expanded with richer preset previews, AI-generated custom datasets, and live data plugins (System Metrics and US Weather) that continuously write data on a schedule. A new line protocol validator provides real-time schema previews and inline error highlighting before writing. Finally, database and table retention periods are now viewable and editable directly in the UI, eliminating the need to use the API or CLI.

recent_posts.title: From Edge to Enterprise: How Litmus and InfluxDB Are Modernizing the Industrial Data Stack
recent_posts.summary: InfluxData and Litmus have announced a strategic partnership to modernize industrial data infrastructure. Litmus Edge provides 250+ prebuilt connectors to OT systems (PLCs, SCADA, CNC, sensors) and handles data normalization and contextualization at the edge, while InfluxDB 3 Enterprise serves as the centralized time series data hub. Together they address limitations of legacy data historians — poor context retention, high-frequency ingest bottlenecks, and expensive cross-site analytics. The architecture supports buffered store-and-forward for intermittent connectivity, unlimited cardinality, and cost-efficient long-term storage via object storage, enabling predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, and industrial AI use cases.

recent_posts.title: Litmus and InfluxData Partner to Power Scalable Industrial AI at the Edge
recent_posts.summary: InfluxData and Litmus have announced a strategic partnership integrating InfluxDB 3 Enterprise with the Litmus Edge Industrial Data Platform. The integration targets industrial organizations needing to collect, process, and analyze high-resolution time series data at the edge. Key capabilities include massive-scale data ingestion in milliseconds, 250+ native OT connectors for industrial systems, context-rich data modeling, efficient long-term storage via object storage compression, and seamless edge-to-cloud replication. The combined solution aims to replace traditional industrial historians and enable real-time predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, and Industrial AI at the edge. Cloud deployments are supported via Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB on AWS.

recent_posts.title: Setting Up an MQTT Data Pipeline with InfluxDB
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to building an MQTT data pipeline that centralizes IoT/sensor telemetry into InfluxDB 3. Covers installing and configuring Eclipse Mosquitto as the MQTT broker, setting up publishing clients, installing InfluxDB 3 Core, and configuring Telegraf as the bridge between MQTT and InfluxDB. Includes topic parsing and pivot processing in Telegraf for a clean data model, plus an overview of why InfluxDB's time-series optimizations (sub-10ms queries, gap-fill functions, retention policies) make it well-suited for high-volume MQTT workloads.

recent_posts.title: From Edge to Cloud: How Litmus Edge and InfluxDB Unlock Industrial Intelligence at Hannover Messe
recent_posts.summary: Litmus Edge and InfluxDB 3 form a reference architecture for industrial data pipelines, addressing the fragmentation of OT environments (PLCs, SCADA, Modbus, OPC-UA) by normalizing and contextualizing machine data at the edge before storing it in InfluxDB for high-frequency ingest, low-latency querying, and fleet-wide analytics. The stack extends to the cloud via Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB, enabling integration with AWS Lambda, Kinesis, and SageMaker. The architecture is being demonstrated end-to-end at Hannover Messe 2026.

recent_posts.title: What’s New in InfluxDB 3 Explorer 1.7: Table Management, Data Import, Transforms, and More
recent_posts.summary: InfluxDB 3 Explorer 1.7 introduces several UI-driven features for managing time series data. A new Manage Tables page lets users view, create, and delete tables with explicit schema control. An Import from InfluxDB workflow enables guided migration of data from InfluxDB v1, v2, or v3 instances, including a dry-run preview and live progress tracking. A new Transform Data section provides a visual interface for setting up automatic ingestion-time transformations — renaming tables or columns, converting values, filtering rows/columns, and downsampling high-frequency data into aggregated summaries — all powered by the Processing Engine without requiring manual plugin configuration.

recent_posts.title: InfluxDB Q1 2026 product updates across Telegraf, InfluxDB 3 and managed offerings
recent_posts.summary: InfluxData's Q1 2026 product recap covers several major updates across their ecosystem. Telegraf Controller enters beta with centralized configuration management, fleet-wide health visibility, RBAC, and API token management. InfluxDB 3.9 improves operational control with better CLI support, resource management, and a beta performance preview featuring optimized queries and reduced CPU/memory usage. The Processing Engine gains new plugins for MQTT, Kafka, AMQP, and OPC UA ingestion, plus batch write support and async request handling. Cloud Dedicated customers get Query History (GA) and S3 API dashboards. InfluxDB Enterprise 1.12.3 delivers 100x faster retention enforcement, 30% lower CPU during compaction, and 5x faster backups. Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB now supports up to 15-node clusters with seamless migration from Core to Enterprise.

recent_posts.title: New Plugins, Faster Writes, and Easier Configuration: What’s New with the InfluxDB 3 Processing Engine
recent_posts.summary: InfluxDB 3's Processing Engine has received several updates including new beta plugins for data ingestion (MQTT, Kafka, AMQP subscribers), OPC UA integration for industrial environments, an import plugin for migrating from older InfluxDB versions, and a schema validator plugin. Engine improvements include synchronous writes with durability control, batch writes for higher throughput, and asynchronous request handling for concurrent execution. InfluxDB 3 Explorer now offers form-based UI configuration for select plugins, replacing manual parameter assembly.

recent_posts.title: What’s New in InfluxDB 3.9: More Operational Control and a New Performance Preview
recent_posts.summary: InfluxDB 3.9 is now available with a focus on operational maturity and system transparency. Key improvements include expanded CLI support for headless/automated environments, increased default string field limit to 1MB, cleaner database lifecycle management (triggers decommissioned on DB removal), and upgrades to DataFusion and bundled Python for better query execution and plugin security. A beta performance preview is available in InfluxDB 3 Enterprise, featuring optimized single-series queries, resource smoothing during compaction/ingestion bursts, wide-and-sparse table support, and automatic distinct value caches. The beta is flag-gated and intended for staging/development environments only, with GA features planned for versions 3.10 and 3.11.

recent_posts.title: Telegraf Enterprise Beta is Now Available: Centralized Control for Telegraf at Scale
recent_posts.summary: InfluxData has launched the Telegraf Enterprise beta, a commercial offering for organizations running Telegraf at scale. It introduces two key components: Telegraf Controller, a UI and API control plane for centralized configuration management and fleet health visibility, and Telegraf Enterprise Support for production-grade assistance. The controller supports pull-based config delivery, bulk operations, label-based organization, and works independently of InfluxDB. A free tier with pre-defined limits is available, while the paid tier bundles the controller with enterprise support. The beta is open to all Telegraf users, with InfluxData seeking feedback from teams managing large agent fleets.

top_posts.title: Microservices to Monolith, Rebuilding Our Backend in Rust
top_posts.summary: InfluxData's platform team migrated their core account and resource management APIs from Go microservices to a Rust monolith to reduce complexity and improve maintainability. They used a strangler fig migration pattern to migrate endpoints one by one without downtime, implementing hexagonal architecture with domain-driven design. The team of five completed the project in three months, achieving safer software through Rust's type system and faster development cycles.

top_posts.title: Introducing the New Cloud Dedicated Admin UI
top_posts.summary: InfluxData has released a major update to the Cloud Dedicated Admin UI, introducing live cluster observability dashboards with CPU, memory, and request rate metrics. The update includes redesigned navigation for quick access to databases, tables, and tokens, plus enhanced table schema browsing with column type filtering. Users can now monitor cluster performance across different time periods and switch between multiple accounts and clusters directly from the interface.

top_posts.title: Is an Air Fryer More Energy Efficient Than an Oven
top_posts.summary: Comparing an air fryer and a conventional oven, this post explores which appliance is more energy-efficient. The analysis includes cooking times, energy consumption during and after warm-up, as well as the financial implications of purchasing an air fryer. While air fryers consume less energy overall because of shorter cooking times and no warm-up requirement, the savings may not justify the purchase cost in the short term. The oven, despite using more energy to warm up, is better insulated and uses energy more efficiently during longer cooking periods.

top_posts.title: A Detailed Guide to C# TimeSpan
top_posts.summary: Learn about the C# TimeSpan struct and how it can improve the readability and robustness of your code. Discover the benefits of using TimeSpan over other alternatives and explore various ways to obtain a TimeSpan in C#. Also, find out about key methods and properties associated with TimeSpan, different ways to format a TimeSpan, and common issues to avoid.

top_posts.title: InfluxData
top_posts.summary: Telegraf 1.37 introduces new plugins for querying Grafana Loki (LogQL), Prometheus (PromQL), NFTables monitoring, and system time metrics. New outputs include ARC-DB and heartbeat endpoints, plus secret stores for Google Cloud and HashiCorp Vault. The release emphasizes a shift toward strict environment variable handling by default in v1.38.0, requiring users to verify configurations. Additional improvements include IP filtering for socket listeners, removal of deprecated options, and persistent self-signed certificates for OPCUA plugins.
